reasoning_traces.think:
The WR1 suppression index is defined as the difference between league-average EPA and a shrunk version of EPA for a given defense. This is a Bayesian shrinkage estimator that adjusts for small-sample bias in per-defense EPA estimates. The funnel multiplier redistributes EPA to WR2/WR3/TE based on relative suppression. Penalty reliability coefficients reflect the stability of procedural vs coverage penalties, with procedural penalties having higher reliability due to their consistency across teams. The xgboost model uses a fixed set of game-state features to predict pass probability without incorporating a two-stage structure. Each primitive operates under distinct assumptions: shrinkage assumes normality and homoscedasticity, reliability assumes stationarity, and xgboost assumes feature relevance. Failure modes include overfitting in xgboost, instability in low-volume penalty data, and misalignment between WR1 ranking and suppression estimation.
